# Command reference

Every `sm` command with its flags, generated from the program itself. Run `sm <command> --help` for the same text in your terminal.

## sm

SuperMgmt: manage your infrastructure

```text
sm
```

Flags:

- `--config` (string): path to the configuration file
- `--json` (bool): machine-readable JSON output
- `--log-level` (string, default `info`): log level: debug|info|warn|error

### sm admin

Administer a server through its admin socket (root or the service user)

```text
sm admin
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm admin bootstrap-code

Issue a one-time code for the first administrator and print it

Issues a new one-time bootstrap code and prints only the code on stdout. Any unconsumed code is invalidated. It works while the server has no administrator, and during a restore hold.

```text
sm admin bootstrap-code
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm admin grant

Bind a role to an identity (recovery when no administrator can log in)

```text
sm admin grant <identity-id> <role>
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm admin restore-complete

End the restore hold after reviewing sm doctor and the interrupted jobs

```text
sm admin restore-complete
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

### sm apps

List, inspect and create applications and their targets

```text
sm apps
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm apps create

Create an application

Create an application from a JSON request (--file, the body of POST /apps) and/or flags. A flag the
command line sets wins over the same field in the file. The Compose file is the control-plane source and may
hold ${secret:<ref>} references, never a secret value.

```text
sm apps create [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--automation-identity` (bool): link the GitHub Actions automation identity
- `--compose-file` (string): Compose file to keep as the control-plane source
- `--deployed-service` (string): the Compose service CI deploys
- `--file` (string): JSON file with the create request
- `--manifest-path` (string): path of the manifest in the repository
- `--name` (string): app name
- `--ref` (stringArray): secret reference NAME=secret://apps/... (repeatable)
- `--var` (stringArray): Compose variable NAME=value (repeatable)

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm apps get

Show one application with its targets (id or name)

```text
sm apps get <app>
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm apps list

List applications

```text
sm apps list [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--cursor` (string): continue after this cursor
- `--limit` (int): maximum items per page (default 50, max 500)

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm apps target

Manage where an application runs

```text
sm apps target
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

##### sm apps target add

Bind an application to an environment and a node

Add a target: the application in one environment on one node. The Compose project is derived by the
daemon (sm-<app>-<environment>). The deployment policy comes from --policy-file (JSON) and/or flags; a flag
the command line sets wins over the file.

```text
sm apps target add <app> [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--bind-address` (stringArray): address a published port may bind (repeatable)
- `--environment` (string): environment name
- `--node` (string): node (id or name)
- `--policy-file` (string): JSON file with the deployment policy
- `--rollback` (string): rollback mode: automatic | manual
- `--stateful` (bool): the application holds state

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

### sm backup

Create and list backups; restore one offline

```text
sm backup
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm backup create

Create a backup now (a job; master keys are never included)

Create a backup archive. Online it is a job the server runs.

With --offline the service must be stopped: the database is opened read-only and copied as it is. Nothing
is migrated, no configuration is activated and nothing is audited or pruned, so the archive keeps the
schema version of the database (the upgrade relies on it). The archive belongs to the user running this.

```text
sm backup create [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--offline` (bool): back up a stopped control plane read-only, without migrating it

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm backup list

List the backup archives with the master keys they need

```text
sm backup list
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm backup restore

Restore a backup archive into a stopped control plane

Restores a backup archive (.tar.zst) offline: the daemon must be stopped. The restored database starts in restore hold until an admin runs `sm admin restore-complete`. Master keys are never part of an archive: import them first with `sm secrets import-key --offline`.

```text
sm backup restore ARCHIVE [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--offline` (bool): restore without a running daemon (required)

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

### sm deploy

Deploy a commit's images to an application's environment

Request a deployment of the exact commit and image digests CI built. The daemon verifies CI for the
commit, freezes the plan and, when policy asks for it, waits for approval: this command prints that plan
preview. With --wait it blocks until the deployment succeeds, fails or is rolled back.

```text
sm deploy <app> <environment> --commit <sha> --image <service>=<digest> [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--commit` (string): full commit SHA CI built
- `--image` (stringArray): service=sha256:<digest> to deploy (repeatable)
- `--interval` (duration, default `2s`): with --wait: how often to poll
- `--wait` (bool): wait until the deployment settles; exit non-zero unless it succeeded

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

### sm docker

Open lazydocker on a node over SSH

Open lazydocker on the node through an interactive SSH session. SuperMgmt never installs it:
when it is missing on the node, install it there yourself.

```text
sm docker <node> [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--user` (string): log in as this user instead of the node's admin_user

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

### sm doctor

Diagnose configuration, paths and database health

Diagnose this machine. --offline checks the configuration, paths and database files without contacting
the service. Without it, doctor asks a running server what it can tell about itself over its admin
socket (run it as root or the service user); a local installation has no such socket and gets the
offline checks, with a running local daemon reported instead of failed.

```text
sm doctor [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--offline` (bool): check this machine without contacting the daemon

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

### sm enrollments

Issue join tokens for nodes that enroll themselves

```text
sm enrollments
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm enrollments create

Issue a join token (the value is shown once)

Issue a join token for `sm join`. It lives at most 24 hours and can be limited to a number of
nodes, to tags the enrolled nodes receive and to source networks. The token is printed once, alone, on
stdout; the command to run on the node goes to stderr and never contains it.

```text
sm enrollments create [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--expires-in` (string, default `1h`): lifetime, e.g. 30m or 12h (at most 24h)
- `--max-nodes` (int, default `1`): how many nodes may enroll with this token
- `--source-cidr` (stringSlice): network the enrolling node must come from, e.g. 203.0.113.0/24 (repeatable)
- `--tag` (stringSlice): tag given to every node that enrolls with this token (repeatable)

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

### sm join

Enroll this node with a SuperMgmt server (run as root)


Flags:

### sm login

Sign in to a remote server

Sign in to the server of the current profile with your identity provider. By default a browser opens
and the provider redirects back to a loopback port; --device shows a code to enter on another device.
The session token is kept in the OS credential store (a 0600 file when none is usable), never printed.

Providers with a confidential client (such as Dex) need a registered redirect: pass --callback-port.
--bootstrap exchanges the one-time code of `sm admin bootstrap-code` (read from the terminal or stdin);
on a server with OIDC, sign in normally first, then run --bootstrap. Without OIDC the administrator is created
by name: --display-name, or a prompt (prefilled from $USER) on a terminal. --token-stdin stores an API token.

```text
sm login [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--bootstrap` (bool): exchange a one-time bootstrap code for the first administrator
- `--callback-port` (int): loopback port for the browser redirect (default: a random free one)
- `--device` (bool): use the device authorization grant instead of a browser redirect
- `--display-name` (string): name of the first administrator (--bootstrap on a server without OIDC)
- `--no-browser` (bool): print the URL instead of opening a browser
- `--profile` (string): profile to sign in to (default: the current one)
- `--token-stdin` (bool): store an API token read from the terminal or stdin

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

### sm logout

Sign out: revoke the session on the server and forget the stored credential

```text
sm logout [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--profile` (string): profile to sign out of (default: the current one)

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

### sm mcp

Serve MCP over stdio as a registered MCP client

Serve the Model Context Protocol on stdin and stdout, for an MCP host to launch.

The server authenticates with the token that `sm mcp clients add` stored, read from
--token-file or the OS keychain (--keychain), never from arguments or the environment.
Standard output carries only JSON-RPC; diagnostics go to standard error.

```text
sm mcp (--token-file FILE | --keychain NAME) [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--keychain` (string): OS keychain entry holding the MCP client token
- `--token-file` (string): file holding the MCP client token (mode 0600, owned by you)

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm mcp clients

List, add and remove MCP clients

```text
sm mcp clients
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

##### sm mcp clients add

Register a local MCP client and store its one-time token

Register a local MCP client. When policy requires approval, this prints the job to approve and stops;
run the same command again after `sm jobs approve <job> --plan-hash <hash>` to issue the token. The token goes straight
into --token-file (created exclusively, mode 0600) or the OS keychain (--keychain). It is never printed
and cannot be shown again.

```text
sm mcp clients add <name> (--token-file FILE | --keychain NAME) [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--expires` (string, default `90d`): token lifetime, e.g. 90d (at most 365d)
- `--keychain` (string): OS keychain entry that receives the token (must not exist)
- `--token-file` (string): file that receives the token (must not exist)

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

##### sm mcp clients list

List MCP clients (their tokens are never shown)

```text
sm mcp clients list
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

##### sm mcp clients remove

Remove an MCP client and revoke its token

```text
sm mcp clients remove <name|id>
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

### sm nodes

List, add, inspect and probe nodes

```text

```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm nodes add

Add an SSH node (or this machine with --local)

Add an SSH node. The host key is scanned and its SHA256 fingerprint shown; nothing is
trusted until you confirm it: pass --fingerprint SHA256:... (verified out of band) or type
'yes' at the prompt. The confirmed key is pinned for every later connection.

```text
sm nodes add [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--admin-credential-ref` (string): your credential for admin-user (default ssh-agent://default)
- `--admin-user` (string): your own account on the node (e.g. root or a personal login)
- `--credential-ref` (string): automation credential (default secret://ssh/default)
- `--environment` (string): environment name
- `--fingerprint` (string): expected host key fingerprint (SHA256:...)
- `--host` (string): host name or address
- `--local` (bool): register this machine (read-only)
- `--name` (string): node name
- `--port` (int, default `22`): SSH port
- `--tag` (stringSlice): tag (repeatable)
- `--user` (string): automation account (default supermgmt)
- `--yes` (bool): with --local: consent without prompting

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm nodes get

Show one node (id or name)

```text
sm nodes get <node>
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm nodes list

List nodes with their latest known state

List nodes with their latest known state. With --tree, show every node grouped by provider and, for
Proxmox, each cluster node with its VMs and containers; the filters apply and paging is followed.

```text
sm nodes list [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--cursor` (string): continue after this cursor
- `--environment` (string): only nodes in this environment
- `--limit` (int): maximum items per page (default 50, max 500)
- `--reachability` (string): only nodes with this reachability
- `--tag` (string): only nodes with this tag
- `--tree` (bool): group nodes by provider; Proxmox guests under their cluster node

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm nodes power

Power a Proxmox VM or container (a job; stop needs approval)

Plan the power action, show what policy says, and submit it once you confirm.

start boots the guest, shutdown asks its OS to stop, reboot restarts it. stop cuts the power at once
without a clean shutdown: it is high risk and waits for approval where policy asks for it.

With --wait, stay until the job ends (a job waiting for approval keeps you waiting): exit status 0 when
it succeeded.

```text
sm nodes power <node> <start|shutdown|reboot|stop> [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--wait` (bool): wait until the job ends
- `--yes` (bool): do not ask for confirmation

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.


Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm nodes remove

Retire a node (its history is kept)

```text
sm nodes remove <node> [flags]
```

Flags:

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm nodes repin

Trust the host key a node presents now (after a legitimate change)

Re-pin a node to the host key it presents now. The new key is scanned and both fingerprints are shown;
nothing changes until you confirm: pass --fingerprint SHA256:... (verified out of band) or type 'yes'.
Never confirm a key you cannot account for: a changed host key is also what an attack looks like.

```text
sm nodes repin <node> [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--fingerprint` (string): the new host key's fingerprint (SHA256:...), verified out of band

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm nodes setup

Provision the dedicated supermgmt account on a node (a job; may wait for approval)

Run node.setup: create the supermgmt account on the node over your own admin account (root, or passwordless
sudo), authorize the instance SSH key, grant systemctl on the units it may manage, and verify the result over
a fresh session as that account. Re-run it after `sm ssh-key rotate` to authorize the new key.

--unit grants systemctl on a unit: --unit nginx.service allows start, stop and restart; --unit
nginx.service:restart only restart. Repeat it per unit; the list replaces the node's current grants.
Without --unit a re-run keeps the grants the node has; --no-units removes them all.

Docker access is explicit: it is off unless you pass --docker-access, and it is root-equivalent on the node.

```text
sm nodes setup <node> [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--docker-access` (bool): also give the account docker access (root-equivalent on the node)
- `--logs-mode` (string, default `journal-group`): how logs are read: journal-group or broker
- `--no-units` (bool): remove every unit grant
- `--unit` (stringArray): grant systemctl on a unit: <unit>[:start,stop,restart] (repeatable)
- `--yes` (bool): do not ask for confirmation

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

### sm profile

Manage the servers sm talks to

```text
sm profile
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm profile add

Add a profile for a remote server (or for a local daemon with --local)

Add a profile. A remote profile needs the server's https URL; --ca-file adds a private CA to the system
roots. Sign in with `sm login`. The first profile becomes the current one.

```text
sm profile add <name> [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--ca-file` (string): PEM file with an extra CA to trust (absolute path)
- `--config-file` (string): with --local: the daemon's configuration file (default: the standard location)
- `--local` (bool): a local daemon profile instead of a remote one
- `--url` (string): server URL, `https://host[:port]`
- `--use` (bool): make it the current profile

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm profile list

List profiles and whether you are signed in to each

```text
sm profile list
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm profile remove

Remove a profile and its stored credential (sign out first to end the session on the server)

```text
sm profile remove <name>
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm profile use

Make a profile the current one

```text
sm profile use <name>
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

### sm providers

List, inspect, refresh and check providers

```text
sm providers
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm providers check

Check a Proxmox provider with the service stopped

With a provider name, read the provider from the configuration file and its API token from the secret
store, then connect to the cluster and read its nodes, guests and storages. The service must be stopped.

With --tls-only, connect to the endpoint and verify the certificate it serves against the CA file for the
endpoint's host name. The connection goes through the same outbound filter as the provider client. The installer runs it before any token exists.

Exit status: 0 when the check passes, 8 when it fails.

```text
sm providers check --offline (<name> | --tls-only --endpoint URL --ca-file FILE) [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--ca-file` (string): with --tls-only: the CA that must have signed the certificate
- `--endpoint` (string): with --tls-only: the endpoint to verify, `https://host[:port]`
- `--offline` (bool): check with the service stopped (required)
- `--tls-only` (bool): only verify the certificate the endpoint serves

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm providers get

Show one provider (id or name)

```text
sm providers get <provider>
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm providers list

List providers with their sync status

```text
sm providers list
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm providers refresh

Discover a provider now instead of at the next sync

Run a discovery of the provider now and show how it ended. Nothing is changed on the cluster: only what
SuperMgmt knows about it. Exit status: 0 when the sync worked, 8 when the cluster could not be read.

```text
sm providers refresh <provider>
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

### sm rollback

Redeploy the last known-good deployment of an application's environment

Request a rollback of the newest deployment of the target to its newest earlier known-good one
(--to picks another known-good deployment of the same target). The daemon freezes the known-good
snapshot; no CI gate applies.

```text
sm rollback <app> <environment> [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--interval` (duration, default `2s`): with --wait: how often to poll
- `--to` (string): known-good deployment id to roll back to
- `--wait` (bool): wait until the deployment settles; exit non-zero unless it succeeded

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

### sm secrets

Import secrets and manage the master keys

Secret values and passphrases are read from the terminal (no echo) or from standard input, never from
an argument or an environment variable. Every online operation is the high-risk secret.write action:
policy usually parks it as a job waiting for approval.

```text
sm secrets
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm secrets export-key

Back up a master key as a passphrase-protected file

Export a master key (SMKEY1) wrapped under a passphrase of at least 12 characters, read from the terminal
or standard input. Without --execute this only requests the export: policy parks it as a job that exports
nothing. After it is approved, run the command again with --execute to receive the file, once, within 24h.
If policy needs no approval, --execute exports at once. The export is served on the local-mode socket only.

With --offline (the way on a server) nothing is requested: the service must be stopped, and the key file is
read directly under the database lock.

```text
sm secrets export-key <kek-id> [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--execute` (bool): execute an approved export request (asks for the passphrase)
- `--offline` (bool): export from the key directory with the service stopped
- `--out` (string): write the export to this new file (mode 0600); default: stdout, if it is not a terminal

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm secrets import

Store a secret value as the next version of a named secret

Store a secret value, read from the terminal (no echo), from standard input or from a file with --from-file
(which must not be readable by others). The value is sealed on the server and never shown again.

With --offline (for a value the server needs before any administrator exists, such as the OIDC client
secret or a provider token) nothing is requested: the service must be stopped, and the value is sealed with
the active master key straight into the database. With --from-file, --delete-source unlinks the file once
the value is committed, and only then.

```text
sm secrets import [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--delete-source` (bool): with --offline --from-file: delete the file once the value is committed
- `--from-file` (string): read the value from this file (mode 0600) instead of the terminal or stdin
- `--name` (string): secret name, e.g. providers/pve/token
- `--offline` (bool): store the value with the service stopped, without an administrator

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm secrets import-key

Install a master key from an export file (offline)

Install a master key from an SMKEY1 export, with the service stopped. It needs no database: the key waits as
<kek-id>.key.pending until a restore validates it, or is verified and activated at once when the database
here already references it. The passphrase is read from the terminal or standard input.

```text
sm secrets import-key [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--from` (string): the export file
- `--offline` (bool): install the key without a running service (required)

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm secrets keys

List the master key ids (never the keys)

List the master keys the server knows: the ids to give to export-key and retire-key, which one is active,
and whether the daemon holds each. Key material is never shown.

```text
sm secrets keys
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm secrets retire-key

Delete an old master key that nothing references any more

Delete an old master key file. It refuses while a secret, a backup archive or a running backup still uses it.
Backups copied elsewhere are unknown to SuperMgmt: --external-backups-handled records that you re-made or
discarded them.

```text
sm secrets retire-key <kek-id> [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--external-backups-handled` (bool): acknowledge that copies of backups kept elsewhere were re-made or discarded
- `--yes` (bool): do not ask for confirmation

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm secrets rotate-master-key

Create a new master key and rewrap every secret under it

```text
sm secrets rotate-master-key [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--yes` (bool): do not ask for confirmation

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

### sm server

Run the SuperMgmt server (the systemd service)

```text
sm server
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm server init

Create the database and the master key of a server that is not running

Create or update the database and create the first master key, with the service stopped. Run it as the
service user so the files belong to it. It is safe to repeat: an initialized server is left as it is.

```text
sm server init
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

### sm ssh

Open an interactive shell on a node with your own SSH credentials

Open an interactive shell on a node as its admin_user (override with --user). The session is
audited, and OpenSSH runs with your ssh_config ignored and only the node's pinned host key trusted.

```text
sm ssh <node> [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--user` (string): log in as this user instead of the node's admin_user

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

### sm ssh-key

Show or rotate the instance SSH identity

```text
sm ssh-key
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm ssh-key rotate

Create a new version of the instance SSH key (a job; may wait for approval)

Create a new version of the instance SSH identity. Nodes keep the version they were set up with until
`sm nodes setup <node>` runs again and authorizes the new key.

```text
sm ssh-key rotate [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--yes` (bool): do not ask for confirmation

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm ssh-key show

Print the public key SuperMgmt authenticates with (node setup authorizes it)

```text
sm ssh-key show
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

### sm status

Show the daemon identity, node reachability and pending work

```text
sm status
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

### sm tokens

List, create and revoke API tokens

```text
sm tokens
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm tokens create

Create an API token (the value is shown once)

Create an API token for automation. It can only narrow what you may do: --scope lists action patterns,
empty means all of yours. Expiry is mandatory and at most 365 days. The value is printed once, on stdout.

```text
sm tokens create [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--expires-at` (string): expiry as an RFC 3339 time, instead of --expires-in
- `--expires-in` (string, default `90d`): lifetime, e.g. 30d or 720h (at most 365d)
- `--name` (string): a name for the token (unique among yours)
- `--scope` (stringSlice): action pattern the token is limited to (repeatable)

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm tokens list

List your API tokens (their values are never shown again)

```text
sm tokens list
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

#### sm tokens revoke

Revoke an API token (it stops working on its next request)

```text
sm tokens revoke <token-id>
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

### sm tui

Open the terminal UI

Open the terminal UI (also what plain `sm` does in an interactive terminal).

```text
sm tui
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.

### sm version

Print version, commit, build date, Go version and platform

```text
sm version
```

Also accepts the global flags `--config`, `--json`, `--log-level`.
